# Drafter notes — cid-tiradas-134-136

37 units (tirada 134: 7; tirada 135: 23; tirada 136: 7), 94 verses incl. 3009b and 3014b. `t` cut by script
from packet.md (scratchpad build_units.py); checked: verses complete and in order, `l` line counts = `t`, no
unit crosses 2984/2985 or 3042/3043, JSON valid. Name kept as the default; titleEn "Cid" without cedilla, as 131/132-133.

Rubrics checked on the scan (PDF 315, 316, 319): all three as in the establish LOG.
Footnotes read on the scan (PDF 316–321) and quoted Spanish + English in the notes: 2972, 2982, 2988, 2994,
2997, 3002, 3004, 3005, 3008 (on our 3009), 3011 (on our 3012), 3026, 3028, 3030, 3041, 3042, 3047, 3049, 3058-59.

## Readings for the reviewer to check
1. **sín salve Dios (2990, 3042)**: read sí + me, as at 2960 in 132-133. Pidal's own note to 3042 now supports it:
   "fazer, verbo vicario: 'me pesa, así me salve Dios'". Said in both notes. (This also strengthens the 2960 note
   in the published 132-133, which called it uncertain — for the owner, not changed.)
2. **sí fago (3042)**: rendered "It grieves me indeed" in `i`, following Pidal's 'me pesa' (vicarious fazer);
   `l` "yes I-do".
3. **2983 assi lo ivan penssando**: "they were minding it" (penssar 'see to'); subject unstated; marked as
   less certain in the note.
4. **3023 buenas conpañas que assí an tal señor**: "fine companies, as befits men who have such a lord";
   the loose que makes the turn uncertain — said in the note.
5. **2993 o no irâ mi cort**: irâ = ir + a, both infinitives governed by quisiesse.
6. **3014 èl** (grave): rendered "he who"; no comment on the grave beyond "as printed".
7. **3053–54**: one [va] governing entra[r] and posa[r].
8. **3058-59 acordados**: Pidal's 'preparados' followed; Hinard's 'avertis' and Bello/Adam/Bertoni's
   'juntarse' quoted from his note.
9. **Names**: Anrric/Arric "Enrique", Remond, Fróila (Pidal's note writes Fruela), Birbón, Álvar Díaz, Oca,
   Grañón — Pidal's notes only refer to pp. 19 and 23 of his introduction, which I did not consult (outside the
   allowed aids); so no historical identification is given, and "padre del buen enperador" (3003) is left
   unnamed ("the notes here do not name him"). If the owner allows the introduction pages (printed 19, 23–24 =
   PDF 23, 27–28), these could be filled in. Per Ansuórez identified with Pidal's "conde Pedro Ansúrez",
   Gonzalo's brother (note 3008) — the identification of the line's Per Ansuórez with that count is my inference
   from the note, stated as such ("by Pidal's note").
10. Gonçal[v]o A[n]su[ó]rez rendered "Gonzalo Ansúrez" in `i` (the patronymic is in the line); house "Count Don
    Gonzalo" mentioned in the note.
